## What does this table tell us? {#l2-opening-table}

A survey records the number of pets in **50 households**.

| Number of pets, $x$ | Frequency, $f$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | 15 |
| 1 | <span class="frequency-focus">20</span> |
| 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 1 |

::: {.takeaway}
What does the highlighted **20** represent?
:::
<p class="booklet-cue">Example 3.4 dataset · Booklet p. 39</p>

::: notes
After the title and objective slides, begin the teaching with the familiar two-column frequency table. Students have met frequency tables and histograms in Years 9–10. The 20 is the number of households with exactly one pet. Collect the interpretation without adding another question or suggesting a cumulative interpretation of the highlighted frequency. Keep the distinction between number of pets and number of households explicit.
:::
